title: Freelancer and gig-worker finances — taxes and irregular income
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Freelance and gig income is taxable even without a Form 16. Track every payment, keep invoices and bank proof, and file the right ITR (often ITR-3 or ITR-4 under presumptive taxation for eligible professionals). If your tax liability for the year is above ₹10,000 after TDS, you generally must pay advance tax in instalments through the year; late payment attracts interest. Because income is irregular, work out a baseline monthly spend, keep a larger emergency fund (6–12 months), and set aside a fixed percentage of each payment for tax before you spend it. Open a separate account for business income, and consider health and term insurance since there is no employer cover. A chartered accountant can help for the first year.
summary_hinglish: Freelance aur gig income par bhi tax lagta hai. Har payment ka record aur invoice rakho. Saal ki tax liability ₹10,000 se zyada ho to advance tax instalments mein bharna hota hai. Income irregular hai to 6-12 mahine ka emergency fund rakho aur har payment ka ek hissa tax ke liye alag nikalo.
summary_hi: फ्रीलांस और गिग आय पर भी टैक्स लगता है। हर भुगतान का रिकॉर्ड और इनवॉइस रखें। साल की टैक्स देनदारी ₹10,000 से ज़्यादा हो तो एडवांस टैक्स किस्तों में भरना होता है। आय अनियमित हो तो 6-12 महीने का आपातकालीन फंड रखें और हर भुगतान का हिस्सा टैक्स के लिए अलग रखें।
